segments.text: Let's listen to those ideas and agree on what we can do together to put them in practice. Because ultimately the true measure of the success of this summit will not be in how many declarations we will release, but it will be in what will change in the lives of young Africans because we came together. Excellencies, distinguished guests, once again thank you for your attention and we wish you all a very productive YouthConnekt Africa Summit 2026.
Thank you very much, Honourable Minister. Thank you, Mr Gwet. Another round of applause, please.

The United Nations Development Programme has been an integral part of YouthConnekt from the very beginning. So ladies and gentlemen, please help me to welcome Dr Matthias Naab, the Director of the UNDP Regional Service Centre for Africa and Co-Chair of YouthConnekt Africa. Sir, the floor is yours.

Your Excellency Paul Kagame, President of the Republic of Rwanda. Your Excellency Alexandre Baron-Chamrier, Vice President of the Republic of Gabon. Your Excellency Samuel Matecani, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Lesotho.

Your Excellencies, Heads of State and Government. Honourable Ministers from across the continent. Distinguished representatives of the African Union on behalf of the AU Directorate for Women, Gender and Youth.
Excellencies, Ambassadors and Members of the Diplomatic Corps. Distinguished Development Partners and Private Sector Leaders. Young African Leaders, Entrepreneurs and Innovators.

Ladies and gentlemen, good morning, bonjour, waratunse, wese. It is a great honour to join you here in Kigali for the eighth edition of the YouthConnekt Africa Summit, surrounded by the extraordinary energy, ambition and creativity of Africa's young people. At the outset, allow me to convey the warm greetings and best wishes of the UNDP Administrator, who deeply regrets being unable to join us on this important occasion.

On his behalf, I wish to express our sincere appreciation to His Excellency President Paul Kagame for his visionary leadership and longstanding commitment to empowering Africa's youth. I also extend our gratitude to the Government of Rwanda, the African Union, the YouthConnekt Africa Hub and all our partners for making this gathering possible. Nearly a decade ago, YouthConnekt began in Rwanda with a simple but powerful vision.

Connecting Africa's young people to opportunities, institutions and decision makers. Today, it has evolved into a continental movement spanning 39 African countries. Excellencies, distinguished guests, this year's theme, Shaping the Generational Mission, comes at a defining moment for Africa.

With more than 530 million young people, aged 15 to 35, our continent has an extraordinary opportunity to transform its economies and societies. Yet, the world is changing rapidly. Artificial intelligence is redefining industries and jobs.

Climate change is reshaping livelihoods, while geopolitical tensions and economic fragmentation are disrupting markets and investments. Africa's young people are not waiting for the future to arrive. They are already creating it.

Our responsibility is to ensure their ambition is matched by opportunity, investment and supportive institutions. As Frantz Fanon reminded us, and I quote, each generation must, out of relative obscurity, discover its mission, fulfill it or betray it, end of quote. For Africa's young generation, that mission is clear.

Building inclusive economies, harnessing innovation, expanding opportunities across borders and shaping the decisions that affect their future. Ladies and gentlemen, Africa's young people do not simply need programs. They need ecosystems that connect their ideas and ambitions to finance, markets, leadership opportunities and lasting impact.

Looking ahead, three priorities must guide our collective efforts. First, invest in the future of jobs through future-ready skills, digital transformation, green industries and economic diversification. Here in Rwanda, youth connect through the Aguka initiative is supporting young entrepreneurs, entrepreneurship and job creation.

I wish to recognize the European Union for its generous partnership. Across Africa, UNDP's Timbuktu initiative, including the health tech hub here in Kigali and our university innovation ports are helping young innovators turn ideas into scalable businesses. Second, unlock financing and markets for young entrepreneurs and creatives, mobilizing public and private investment.

Over the past two days, UNDP and the youth connect Africa hub brought together 100 young entrepreneurs and traders to develop export action plans and propose solutions to trade barriers under the Africa continental free trade area. And third, give young people a meaningful role in shaping policies and institutions. This is why in October we onboarded the first Africa UNDP Africa youth co-creators council, a group of 11 youth from across the continent that will advise UNDP on its work.

Excellencies, distinguished partners, over the coming days, this summit will bring together young leaders, policymakers, investors and development partners to advance these priorities. But the true measure of our success will not be the number of discussions we hold. It will be the partnerships we establish, the investments we mobilize and the opportunities we create for young Africans.
And to the young people gathered here today, including myself, this is your moment. Take it. You are not merely the beneficiaries of Africa's development.

You are its innovators, entrepreneurs, leaders and change makers. At UNDP, we stand alongside you because Africa's greatest resource is not only what lies beneath its soil. It is the talent, creativity and determination of its people.

Our generational mission is clear to transform that potential into opportunity, that opportunity into prosperity and that prosperity into a more inclusive and sustainable future for all Africans. Together, let us shape that future. Thank you very much.

Thank you, Dr. Nab and thank you to UNDP for making tangible commitments and standing with Africa's youth. Ladies and gentlemen, excellencies, it is now my honor to invite His Excellency Paul Kagame, President of the Republic of Rwanda, to deliver his keynote address and speak directly with the young people gathered here. Your Excellency, the floor is yours.

Please be seated. Excellency Samuel Srafane Matekane, Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Lesotho, Excellency Alexandre Barreau-Chambrière, Vice President of the Gabonese Republic, distinguished leaders, partners, young people, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, allow me to begin by welcoming you all to Kigali. To all our partners, including the United Nations Development Program and the African Union Commission, I thank you for continuing to support YouthConnekt.

Since its inception, this homegrown solution has developed into a successful and continent-wide initiative. This is not by chance. Everyone involved in this partnership brought something real to the table, including every young person in this room.

Collaboration and reciprocity must always define the relationship between leaders and young Africans in everything we do together. Leaders must eliminate barriers with good policies, and youth must take advantage of the opportunities created for them. A recent survey across the continent shows that young Africans today are more optimistic about the future and want to take charge.

That is the right mindset to have, because real success begins when you build the life you want for yourself without waiting for anyone's permission. Everything Africa has managed to build so far has come when we take ownership of our own future. What will sustain those results? It is not wishing for our problems to go away or for the world to stop being indifferent to our struggles.

We need to focus on what we can control, like choosing the right values that define who we are and staying true to them. Every time you hold yourself to a higher standard, you raise the bar for what is possible for everyone around you. That's the power you hold, so you need to use it wisely.

Many of you present here are entrepreneurs solving some of our continent's most pressing challenges. Almost a quarter of Africa's working age population is actively running or starting a business. That's the highest rate globally.

If scaling remains a problem, the story these numbers tell is that ideas and creativity aren't what's missing. Beyond the structural barriers we all know about, we often fail to talk about how working in silos is holding you back. Remember that some of the most transformational companies on this planet were not built in isolation but through collaboration.
They were built from the ground up by individuals who shared a vision. We need you to do the same because we know and trust that you can. Being expected to do more is actually a good problem to have.

Work hard, stay grounded, and the rewards will be waiting for you. As always, it's our job as leaders to support you and once again, thank you for the invitation to be with you today. I look forward to our conversation and I thank you for your kind attention.

Thank you, Excellency. Ladies and gentlemen, another round of applause for His Excellency the President of the Republic of and what we've taken away is quite some strong words, especially that if you hold yourself to a higher standard, you raise the bar for those around you. Those are words that I will carry with me and that I trust that every young person in the room will carry not just throughout this week but as they continue on their mission.
Now Tania, I'm reliably told that there are certain large delegations that have graced YouthConnekt that we may not have recognized. Indeed. Which I'd like to know.

Le Gabon, est-ce que vous êtes ici? Madagascar, are you in the house? Côte d'Ivoire, est-ce que vous êtes dans la pièce? They may just be in the overhaul room. But there's a really big delegation that has been singing all morning. The Kingdom of Lesotho, can we hear you? And on that note, why don't we take a look at the screens and go over to the overflow room where we have large delegations joining us right now live.
